turns.query: The semiannual survey of over-the-counter derivatives publishes two measures for each risk category: outstanding notional amounts and outstanding gross market values, both in millions of USD. Take the latest period present in the table and report its label. For the row covering all risk categories, report outstanding notional and gross market value in USD trillions, the gross market value as a percent of the notional, and the notional divided by the gross market value. Explain what each of the two measures represents and which of them, if either, can be described as the amount at risk in these markets.

Stay in the same period and work with notional amounts. Report the notional for the foreign exchange category, for gold, for foreign exchange including gold, and for commodities. Then sum the notional of these six categories exactly as published: interest rate, foreign exchange including gold, equity, commodities, credit derivatives and other derivatives, and report that sum. Explain what the leftover amount is and what it shows about how these categories are defined.

For the same period compute, for each risk category, gross market value divided by that category's own notional, in percent. Report the value for interest rate, for foreign exchange excluding gold, for equity and for credit derivatives. Then rank only the five headline risk categories that partition the total without overlapping each other: interest rate, foreign exchange excluding gold, equity, credit derivatives and other derivatives. Exclude the containing aggregates and also the commodity sub-breakdown, which sits one level below these categories rather than beside them. Report the single-letter code and the ratio of the highest and of the lowest, breaking a tie by code ascending. Discuss what factors can affect differences in the ratio, what the aggregate table cannot isolate, and why the ranking excludes containing categories.

Finally trace the aggregate ratio over time. Report gross market value as a percent of notional for the all-categories row at 2022-S2 and at 2024-S1. Report total notional at 2022-S2 in USD trillions. Then, from the par yield curve, report the ten-year yield on the last business day of each of those three periods, being 2022-12-30, 2024-06-28 and the last business day of the latest period. Compare the co-movement of the ratio, notional and yield snapshots, and explain what these aggregate endpoints can and cannot establish about the ratio's drivers.
